Communicating the development and support status of a repository
helps both human collaborators and automated tools understand
whether a project is actively maintained,
a work in progress,
or an archived analysis.
The [repostatus.org](https://www.repostatus.org/) project
provides a standardized, machine-readable and human-readable convention
for declaring project status through badges in the repository `README.md`.

### Standard repository statuses

repostatus.org defines eight standardized statuses
spanning both implementation progress and ongoing maintenance commitment:

- **Concept:** Minimal or no implementation has been done yet,
  or the repository is only intended as an example, demo, or proof-of-concept.
- **WIP (Work in Progress):** Initial development is actively underway,
  but the project has not yet reached a stable, usable release
  suitable for general use.
- **Active:** The project has reached a stable, usable state
  and is being actively developed or maintained.
- **Inactive:** The project has reached a stable, usable state
  but is no longer under active feature development;
  bugfixes or maintenance are provided as time allows.
- **Suspended:** Work started,
  but development has paused before reaching a stable release;
  the authors intend to resume work in the future.
- **Abandoned:** Work started but stopped before a stable release;
  the authors do not intend to resume development.
- **Unsupported:** The project reached a stable release
  but all maintenance has ceased;
  a new maintainer may be sought.
- **Moved:** The project has relocated to a new repository URL,
  where development continues.

### Adding a status badge

Place the status badge near the top of your repository `README.md`,
immediately beneath the main title.
The badge links to the corresponding status definition on repostatus.org.

For an active project:

```markdown
[![Project Status: Active - The project has reached a stable, usable state and is being actively developed.](https://www.repostatus.org/badges/latest/active.svg)](https://www.repostatus.org/#active)
```

For a project in initial development:

```markdown
[![Project Status: WIP - Initial development is in progress, but there has not yet been a stable, usable release suitable for the public.](https://www.repostatus.org/badges/latest/wip.svg)](https://www.repostatus.org/#wip)
```

For a completed analysis repository
that is stable but no longer actively adding features:

```markdown
[![Project Status: Inactive - The project has reached a stable, usable state but is no longer being actively developed; support/maintenance will be provided as time allows.](https://www.repostatus.org/badges/latest/inactive.svg)](https://www.repostatus.org/#inactive)
```

### Lifecycle management

Update the status badge as your project evolves through its lifecycle:

1. **Start as Concept or WIP:** Begin new repositories with `Concept`
   (for early prototypes)
   or `WIP` (when building an analysis pipeline or package).
2. **Promote to Active:** Switch to `Active` once the codebase reaches
   a functional, reproducible state with working scripts and tests.
3. **Transition upon project completion:** When an epidemiology study or
   manuscript is published and the analysis code is finalized,
   update the badge to `Inactive` or `Unsupported`
   so readers know whether future bug fixes or dependency updates are planned.
